newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 3-mth CD rate hits 0.55%, highest since Aug.
newsitem.headline: Japan 3-mth CD rate hits 0.55%, highest since Aug.

text.p: The rate on benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) rose to 0.55 percent on Tuesday afternoon in Tokyo, the highest since August 28, 1996, traders said.
The CDs were issued at 0.54 percent on Monday.

The rise in the key CD rate was mainly attributed to continued upward pressure in shorter-term money rates ahead of the end of the current bank reserve reporting period on Friday and before the fiscal year-end on March 31, traders said.
The issuers on Tuesday were said to be some city banks which were aiming at rolling over their maturing CDs.
The issued volume was around 300 billon yen, traders said.
The key overnight call rate was traded at 0.51 percent on Tuesday, up from Monday's weighted average rate of 0.49 percent. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
